parts.note: Easy is a surname here: Jack Easy, hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel, held the junior rank a young naval officer starts at

explanation.surface: An encouraging word that this first clue is a gentle one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective about the clue's difficulty; it is the name in the title of Marryat's novel 'Mr Midshipman Easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young officer cadet in the Royal Navy began at this rank, as Marryat's hero Jack Easy did.

clue.text: What might we make of two thousand and five hundred ?

definitions.text: What might we make of two thousand and five hundred ?

parts.words: What might we make of two thousand and five hundred ?
parts.note: two thousand is MM in Roman numerals and five hundred is D: letters that also stand for military decorations, like MM for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A simple arithmetic puzzle about a large number.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numerals MM and D may be read as initials worn after a name, such as MM (Military Medal).
explanation.definitionFit: Decorations awarded for service, often shown by initials after a soldier's name.

parts.note: a dove is a bird

explanation.surface: A harbour that suits the bird well.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the English Channel port facing France.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry harbour in Kent on the Channel coast.

definitions.meaning: a union call for workers to down tools and walk out

explanation.surface: A notice announcing a strike is passed round.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes things round, and a union official's cry calling everyone out on strike.

definitions.meaning: a rice field, a place for growing the crop
British informal for a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A temper that is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing' looks like an adjective on 'rage'; it is the rice field where the crop grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A flooded field for cultivating rice, and a fit of temper.

clue.text: Plant is a creeper — worth being pruned

parts.note: a snake creeps along the ground, so an adder

indicators.note: pruning cuts something back, so the last letter of worth is lopped off

explanation.surface: A climbing plant is worth cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeper' suggests a climbing plant; it is the snake. 'being pruned' cuts WORTH to WORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adderwort is a name for bistort, a herbaceous plant with a twisted root.

definitions.meaning: the book of the Bible recording what the Apostles did
turns are performances on a variety bill

explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament book about the Apostles, and the items in a variety show programme.

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
Don is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A romance serial ends on a cliffhanger.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going, so it means persisted.

parts.note: a portrait so lifelike that it seems about to talk is described with this adjective

explanation.surface: An admirer comments on a striking portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'speaking likeness' is a phrase for a portrait so true to life it seems to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait so vivid it seems about to utter a word is called lifelike in this way.

indicators.note: a diversion sends things on another route, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turn off the television for a change of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' rearranges TV AS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the sailors' command to cease or hold.

clue.text: Foresaw requirement-took things on board about six

indicators.note: about means going round, so the eating word is put around the numeral

parts.note: to take food on board is to eat, so dined
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone anticipated what was needed when taking on six items of cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VI inside DINED. 'requirement' joins definition to wordplay: one divines what is required.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to discover by intuition, as a prophet perceives the future.

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so the letters of grieved are scrambled

explanation.surface: Two people drift apart, both deeply upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges GRIEVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that diverge separate, moving away from each other.

parts.note: matches as cricket fixtures at the famous London ground, and the house as the upper chamber of Parliament whose members share its name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there are any matches at home to strike a light.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground where matches are played; the House of Lords is the upper chamber of the British Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers of the upper House share their name with the home of cricket in St John's Wood.

parts.note: the CID is the detective branch, associated with Scotland Yard, so the Yard's
tick is informal British for credit, buying on tick

explanation.surface: A police detective department's financial standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, home of the CID (Criminal Investigation Department).
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring rod one yard long, hence any standard of comparison.

clue.text: Notice dud replacement when taking off

indicators.note: replacement means the letters are put back in different positions, so notice dud is reordered

explanation.surface: A warning that a faulty part was swapped just before an aircraft took off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges NOTICE DUD; the '16' in the held clue is not on the printed page.
explanation.definitionFit: A deduction is a subtraction, an amount taken off a total.

clue.text: Leaves producer to name theatre work

definitions.meaning: a tree or shrub that keeps its foliage all year
the title of a 1930 London musical starring Jessie Matthews

explanation.surface: A theatre producer is asked to name a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in leaf all year round, and the 1930 Rodgers and Hart stage musical of that name.

clue.text: Some impulse behind the craft of James's short novel

definitions.meaning: a rotation of a ship's propeller, which drives the vessel from astern
Henry James's ghost story novella of 1898

explanation.surface: Motivation behind the art of a novelist's brief work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests the writer's art; it is the boat, pushed along by its propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: One rotation of a ship's propeller, and Henry James's ghost story.

parts.note: the Fall is the expulsion of Adam and Eve from the biblical garden, which shares its name with rivers in Cumbria and Kent

explanation.surface: A warning about a river one might tumble into.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fall of Man took place in the garden of Genesis; the Eden is also a river in Cumbria in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Genesis where Adam fell from grace shares its name with an English river.

clue.text: Challenging article by a diminutive Lancastrian

parts.note: John of Gaunt was the founder of the House of Lancaster
-let is a suffix making something small, as in piglet

explanation.surface: A small person from Lancashire is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancastrian' suggests someone from Lancashire; it is John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove thrown down as a challenge to fight.

definitions.meaning: American slang for a contemptible man
a ship's list is its leaning to one side

explanation.surface: An American scoundrel turns up on a roll of names.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a rotter, and a nautical verb meaning to tilt to one side.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps, so RE's
trains are a means of transport

explanation.surface: Inspections of the army corps' vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it.

parts.note: to give money is to pay it
L is the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone paid for a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' is a chairman's or auctioneer's mallet, not a carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mallet used by an auctioneer or judge.

indicators.note: letters from means a run of letters is taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: Long missives written in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lengthy' is read as 'units of length'.
explanation.definitionFit: Measures of length, each a twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: The writer's ending might be unreadable!

definitions.text: The writer's ending might be unreadable!

parts.words: The writer's ending might be unreadable!
parts.note: the name a letter-writer scrawls at the foot of a letter is often illegible

explanation.surface: A complaint that an author's final chapter cannot be read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' suggests the close of a novel; it is the name signed at the bottom of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The autograph closing a letter is notoriously hard to decipher.

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is told to follow the instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' suggests instructions; it gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result.

clue.text: Material found in any London store

indicators.note: found in says the letters are concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fabric on sale in any shop in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to the letters running across 'aNY LONdon'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric used for stockings and other cloth.

clue.text: About everyone has returned, that's plain

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone has come back, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has returned' reverses ON ALL to give LLANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy plain in Spanish America.

clue.text: Near riot about dictionary found in school

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go around the dictionary
riot suggests disorder, so the letters of near are thrown about

parts.note: fodder
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A disturbance over a dictionary in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges NEAR into REAN; 'about' puts it around OED. ROEDEAN is a girls' boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known English independent girls' school on the Sussex coast.

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A seaman's remains lie in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: SALTASH is a town in Cornwall, the south-western tip of England, on the Tamar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cornish town on the River Tamar, so a place found in that county.

definitions.meaning: something that lifts: a bird or aircraft rises on it
an extension or side section of a large building

explanation.surface: A lift installed for one section of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevator' suggests a lift for the building; it is what raises a bird into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: What lifts a bird or plane, and a side section of a large house or hospital.

definitions.meaning: in old medical usage these are disorders or ailments a doctor treats

explanation.surface: Romantic feelings that ought to be handled with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Fond attachments, and an old medical term for diseased conditions needing a doctor.
